To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

L-AP4 binds to the human mGlu ATDs in a similar manner to L-glu, but with a different binding mode, and that both the electronic nature of the phosphate and its steric interactions with residues in the mGlu8 ATD are important for its group III functional potency and subtype selectivity.
the human mGlu ATDs have evolved to recognize L-glu with high specificity and that L-AP4 is an excellent Group III agonist because of the unique way in which it binds to the ATDs of these receptors.
the first crystal structures of L-AP3 bound to the human mGlu1 ATD and the first crystal structures in complex of the human mGul ATD with L-AP4 were solved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of group III mGhu receptor selectivity and functional activity of L-AP3 and L-AP3.
the molecular basis for group selective functional agonists of Group III mGlus.
the molecular basis for the Group III functional agonists potency and selectivity of L-AP3 and L-AP5.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the L-AP4 bound mGlu8 ATD crystal structure provides a molecular basis for L-glu's group III selectivity and L-AP's group III potency and selectivity.
the distal phosphate group of L-AP2 is a key structural determinant of the group selectivity of L-AP3 and that the proximal carboxylate group is a key determinant of its potency.
the L-AP4 distal phosphate is critical for Group III mGhu receptor functional agonism and that the L-2-amino group of L-AP3 and L-AP6 is important for Group II mGlu receptor agonism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have determined the first human mGlus ATD crystal structure in complex with L-AP4 and have provided the structural basis for L-4-AP4's exquisite group III functional selectivity.

the L-AP4 distal phosphate is the key structural element that contributes to L-AP4 group III mGhu receptor functional agonist potency, and the L-AP 4 proximal phosphonate is the key structural determinant that contributes to the exquisite L-AP4 Group III mGhu subtype functional agonist selectivity.

the L-AP4 bound mGlu1 and mGlu8 structures provide the first molecular insights into how the Group III mGlus are functionally activated and how L-AP4 is able to activate all three Group III subtypes with similar functional potency and selectivities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the distal phosphate group of L-AP2 plays a key role in its agonist potency and subtype selectivity, and that the mGlu8 ATD is an ideal model system to further understand the mechanism of group III agonist selectivity and potency.

we solved the first mGlu8 ATD crystal structures in complexed with both L-glu and the group III agonist L-AP4, providing the molecular basis for group III mGhu functional agonist potency, and selectivity.
the ATD of mGlu8 is structurally very similar to the ATD of other mGlu subfamily members.
